item.title: Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for cyberattack on foreign minister
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as foreign minister, said Saturday that hackers had published his personal information on the dark web, citing intimidation as a motive ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for a cyberattack on her foreign minister, after a rise in hybrid disruptions from entities aligned with Vladimir Putin’s government. “The fact that confidential information concerning government officials is being put up for sale is a matter of grave concern and must be addressed with the utmost determination,” Meloni said. Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as foreign minister, said Saturday that hackers had published his personal information on the dark web, citing intimidation as a motive.  “Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted,” he said in a post on X. Tajani has asked for the topic of hybrid wars to be placed at the top of the agenda of a G7 meeting set to take place in Paris on Monday, Ansa reported. Officials close to Tajani said Italy’s cybersecurity apparatus had detected the minister’s personal details in recent days through its monitoring activity, and that they were accompanied by threats and attempts to retrieve more information about him and his family. They said the that because the information was hosted on the dark web, a high degree of anonymity for users accessing it was possible. In screenshots of the dark web pages shared by the officials, similar requests for more information were present for other cybersecurity experts and Italian public officials, including a prosecutor, a police official and a mayor. They are all deemed to be “citizens hostile to the Russian Federation.” The attack on Tajani comes as law enforcement officials report an increase in cyberattacks from hacking groups sympathetic to Russia. Interference has disrupted a range of activities, including mundane operations like funeral homes and supermarket freezers. Meloni’s government is looking into whether outside actors such as Russia had a hand in recent protests that swept Milan and other European cities.  Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov didn’t respond to a request for comment. Italy has been a supporter of Ukraine in its war against Russia since its 2022 invasion.

item.title: SpaceX director Donald Harrison resigns from board a day after US election
item.description: Harrison, who joined SpaceX's board in 2015 as part of Google's investment, stepped down on November 4. The exit comes as independent directors of SpaceX and Tesla consider a potential merger ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Carmen Arroyo SpaceX board member Donald Harrison resigned from the role after more than a decade, leaving the company as a group of independent directors consider a potential merger with Tesla Inc. Harrison informed SpaceX of his intention to resign on Nov. 4, one day after the US midterm election, according to a SpaceX filing issued after the close Friday. The company said his decision was not due to any disagreement with the company. Harrison joined the board in 2015 as part of Google’s investment in Musk’s rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company. He was an independent director and still works for Google parent Alphabet Inc., leading its corporate partnerships and development team. SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to consider a potential combination, Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said last month. There’s a push to announce a deal by the first half of next year so that it closes during this administration, Bloomberg News reported. Musk hasn’t said which board members are on the companies’ special committees. Harrison was among the directors SpaceX considers independent, alongside Ira Ehrenpreis, Roelof Botha, Luke Nosek, Steve Jurvetson and Randy Glein. Alphabet remains one of SpaceX’s leading backers, with the second-biggest shareholding after Musk. The investment weighed on the earnings results Alphabet reported last week due to SpaceX shares declining last quarter. Google and SpaceX have rival AI models and chatbots in Gemini and Grok that compete with Anthropic PBC’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

item.title: Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus
item.description: Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus

Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus Noel Tata retired as Voltas chairman and director on November 11 upon reaching the age of superannuation

Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026 (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 07 2026 | 12:51 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker. Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines. Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing. The Companies Act 2013 mandates that any managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed or continue employment if they are 70 years of age or older.

Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026. He has been associated with Voltas since 2003. Also Read

Additionally, the board has appointed Sunil D'Souza as the new Chairman of Voltas. D'Souza currently leads the Tata Group's FMCG arm, Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL), as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The company sells a wide range of consumer products, including salt, tea, coffee, packaged foods and beverages under brands such as Tata Salt, Tata Tea, Tetley and Tata Sampann. "The Board has appointed Sunil Alaric D'Souza as Chairman of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," Voltas said.

Moreover, the tenure of Voltas Managing Director C P Mukundan Menon will end on May 24, 2027, when he will retire from the company's services in line with the Tata Group's retirement policy for executive directors. The board has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head of the Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director for a five-year term beginning May 25, 2027, subject to shareholders' approval. "As part of a planned succession process, the Board, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head - Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director of the Company for a term of five years commencing from May 25, 2027," Voltas said.

This will be subject to the approval of the shareholders. To ensure a smooth transition, Balan has been redesignated as Head Room Air Conditioner Business and Managing Director Designate until his appointment takes effect. The board has also approved the appointment of Venkatesalu Palaniswamy as an Additional Director in the non-independent, non-executive category with effect from November 12, 2026.

item.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
item.description: State Department's Rewards for Justice programme is offering up to $20 mn and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment and personnel, including nuclear scientists ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme

US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme State Department's Rewards for Justice programme is offering up to $20 mn and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment and personnel, including nuclear scientists

Image Credit: Bloomberg

ANI US 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 07 2026 | 9:39 AM IST

Listen to This Article

The United States military announced on Friday that Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for details concerning Iran's nuclear programme, even as President Donald Trump asserted that Tehran is eager to conclude the ongoing war. In a post shared on X, the United States Central Command stated that a State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear programme, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community." The initiative was originally founded in 1984 under the national security rewards programme managed by the State Department to provide financial incentives for intelligence that safeguards American lives and interests.

Detailing the rationale behind the announcement, the State Department noted that Tehran's non-compliance with its safeguards obligations to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has resulted in the agency losing "continuity of knowledge" concerning the production and inventory of critical elements such as centrifuges, though the directive outlined no precise parameters regarding what intelligence would secure the full $20 million reward. Meanwhile, President Trump has repeatedly claimed that US forces have successfully dismantled Iran's nuclear programme. Speaking in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday evening, the US leader remarked, "If we didn't hit Iran, you wouldn't have Israel today," adding, "If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East."

Despite the military actions, the president pointed out that eight months of conflict have heavily damaged Iran's economy and military, leaving Tehran anxious to make a deal. "We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he stated. Amid these developments, diplomatic efforts involving various mediators have intensified to avert any resumption of fighting. On Tuesday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian affirmed that his administration continues to pursue avenues to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Earlier this week, Trump noted that he still needs to address one or two residual sites, specifically mentioning Pickaxe Mountain, located in central Iran, a suspected nuclear facility whose designation has been strongly denied by Tehran.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
